value="<b><font style="font-size: 15px;">Consistency — the right level per data</font></b><br>-&nbsp; Financial state → STRONG (ACID + unique constraints)<br>-&nbsp; Reconciliation results → STRONG<br>-&nbsp; Dashboards &amp; analytics → EVENTUAL<br><br><i>Not everything needs global strong consistency.</i>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="190" width="450" x="40" y="670" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="xs1qh2Dv-s7SBkDrsczF-64" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=13;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Scale</b><br>Kafka partitions by merchant / txn id → N workers<br>DB partitioned by date, indexed on transaction_id<br>Hot data in DB, old data → data lake<br><i>10M txn/day: add partitions + workers, not a bigger box.</i>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="190" width="450" x="40" y="880" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="xs1qh2Dv-s7SBkDrsczF-65" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=14;fillColor=#f8cecc;strokeColor=#b85450;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>If something fails</b><br>• Worker crashes → Kafka still holds the message → restart → reprocess → gate skips finished work<br>• Source arrives late → WAITING, not "missing"<br>• Kafka down → adapters retry; raw is already saved<br>• Operator error → no direct edits; only validated, audited actions<br>• Wrong match risk → conservative rules + review queue" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="260" width="430" x="530" y="810" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="xs1qh2Dv-s7SBkDrsczF-66" parent="1" value="<b>Exception queue</b><br>exceptions + MEDIUM review items<br>owner · SLA assigned" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="90" width="430" x="1480" y="680" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=1;html=1;endArrow=block;endFill=1;strokeWidth=2;strokeColor=#d79b00;fontSize=11;fontColor=#d79b00;labelBackgroundColor=#ffffff;fontSize=15;fontStyle=1;" target="xs1qh2Dv-s7SBkDrsczF-68" value="⑩"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="xs1qh2Dv-s7SBkDrsczF-72" edge="1" parent="1" source="xs1qh2Dv-s7SBkDrsczF-68" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=1;html=1;endArrow=block;endFill=1;strokeWidth=2;strokeColor=#b85450;fontSize=11;fontColor=#b85450;labelBackgroundColor=#ffffff;fontSize=15;fontStyle=1;exitX=0;exitY=0.5;entryX=1;entryY=0.5;" target="xs1qh2Dv-s7SBkDrsczF-56" value="⑪"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="xs1qh2Dv-s7SBkDrsczF-73" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=16;fontColor=#222222;fontStyle=1;spacing=4;" value="How to read it — follow the numbers" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="30" width="900" x="40" y="1110" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="xs1qh2Dv-s7SBkDrsczF-74" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=12;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<font style="font-size: 15px;"><b style="">Flow (①–⑫)</b><br>① Sources deliver records — different formats, late, duplicated.<br>② Adapter parses, validates, normalizes to ONE canonical model; the raw record is saved untouched.<br>③ Canonical events go to Kafka (key = merchant / txn id).<br>④ Idempotency gate: source + external id already seen? Skip.<br>⑤ Workers run the rule hierarchy: exact ID → composite → time window.<br>⑥ HIGH → MATCHED · MEDIUM → review · LOW / nothing found → wait, then EXCEPTION.<br>⑦ Results are written in ACID transactions. ⑧ Every change → append-only audit.<br>⑨ Exceptions go to humans. ⑩ They propose a validated resolution action. ⑪ It is audited.<br>⑫ Dashboards read an eventually-consistent copy.<br><br><b style="">Example:</b> internal ₹1,000 · gateway ₹1,000 · bank ₹999 → rules match all three by reference, amounts differ → AMOUNT_MISMATCH exception, original untouched.</font>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="420" width="610" x="40" y="1150" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="xs1qh2Dv-s7SBkDrsczF-75" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=15;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Architect decisions — say "why A over B"</b><br>1. Canonical model + adapters, not per-source logic in the engine → the engine never learns formats.<br>2. Raw immutable, normalized derived → audits can replay.<br>3. At-least-once + idempotency, not exactly-once → simpler and safer.<br>4. Rule hierarchy, not one giant algorithm → every match carries a confidence.<br>5. Conservative matching → a false match is worse than an open item.<br>6. Two separate statuses → a SUCCESS payment can still be AMOUNT_MISMATCH.<br>7. Financial events, not overwritten amounts → ₹1,000 − ₹300 refund = ₹700 net, history kept.<br>8. Waiting window, not instant "missing" → event time ≠ processing time.<br>9. Strong consistency only where money lives; eventual for dashboards.<br>10. Humans act through validated actions, never by editing data." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="420" width="610" x="670" y="1150" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="xs1qh2Dv-s7SBkDrsczF-76" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=12;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Mental model &amp; interview close</b><br><i>Source → Canonical → Idempotent → Match by confidence → Decide → Resolve → Audit</i><br><br><b>Trade-offs we accept</b><br>• Conservative matching → more manual exceptions<br>• At-least-once → we pay for duplicate handling<br>• Waiting windows → slower final answers<br>• Strong consistency on the core DB → writes scale by partitioning, not by relaxing guarantees<br><br><b>One-line close:</b> "Reconciliation is a financial consistency engine across independent systems — accuracy over speed, and every decision can be explained from the raw data and the audit trail."<br><br><b>Honest test:</b> if a bank file arrives two days late, does the system say "missing" and raise a false alarm? It must not." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="420" width="630" x="1300" y="1150" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

div.div:
Consistency — the right level per data
- Financial state → STRONG (ACID + unique constraints)
- Reconciliation results → STRONG
- Dashboards & analytics → EVENTUAL
Not everything needs global strong consistency.

div.div:
Scale
Kafka partitions by merchant / txn id → N workers
DB partitioned by date, indexed on transaction_id
Hot data in DB, old data → data lake
10M txn/day: add partitions + workers, not a bigger box.

div.div:
If something fails
• Worker crashes → Kafka still holds the message → restart → reprocess → gate skips finished work
• Source arrives late → WAITING, not "missing"
• Kafka down → adapters retry; raw is already saved
• Operator error → no direct edits; only validated, audited actions
• Wrong match risk → conservative rules + review queue

div.div: How to read it — follow the numbers

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 592px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1396px; margin-left: 30px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span:
Flow (①–⑫)
① Sources deliver records — different formats, late, duplicated.
② Adapter parses, validates, normalizes to ONE canonical model; the raw record is saved untouched.
③ Canonical events go to Kafka (key = merchant / txn id).
④ Idempotency gate: source + external id already seen? Skip.
⑤ Workers run the rule hierarchy: exact ID → composite → time window.
⑥ HIGH → MATCHED · MEDIUM → review · LOW / nothing found → wait, then EXCEPTION.
⑦ Results are written in ACID transactions. ⑧ Every change → append-only audit.
⑨ Exceptions go to humans. ⑩ They propose a validated resolution action. ⑪ It is audited.
⑫ Dashboards read an eventually-consistent copy.
Example: internal ₹1,000 · gateway ₹1,000 · bank ₹999 → rules match all three by reference, amounts differ → AMOUNT_MISMATCH exception, original untouched.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 592px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1396px; margin-left: 660px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 15px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Architect decisions — say "why A over B"
1. Canonical model + adapters, not per-source logic in the engine → the engine never learns formats.
2. Raw immutable, normalized derived → audits can replay.
3. At-least-once + idempotency, not exactly-once → simpler and safer.
4. Rule hierarchy, not one giant algorithm → every match carries a confidence.
5. Conservative matching → a false match is worse than an open item.
6. Two separate statuses → a SUCCESS payment can still be AMOUNT_MISMATCH.
7. Financial events, not overwritten amounts → ₹1,000 − ₹300 refund = ₹700 net, history kept.
8. Waiting window, not instant "missing" → event time ≠ processing time.
9. Strong consistency only where money lives; eventual for dashboards.
10. Humans act through validated actions, never by editing data.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 612px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1396px; margin-left: 1290px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Mental model & interview close
Source → Canonical → Idempotent → Match by confidence → Decide → Resolve → Audit
Trade-offs we accept
• Conservative matching → more manual exceptions
• At-least-once → we pay for duplicate handling
• Waiting windows → slower final answers
• Strong consistency on the core DB → writes scale by partitioning, not by relaxing guarantees
One-line close: "Reconciliation is a financial consistency engine across independent systems — accuracy over speed, and every decision can be explained from the raw data and the audit trail."
Honest test: if a bank file arrives two days late, does the system say "missing" and raise a false alarm? It must not.
